title: C# Questions & Answers - Initialization of Variables
sourceFile: Variables Intialization - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on Initialization of variables in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: Calculation: c = (++a) + (b++). ++a increments 5 to 6 first. b++ uses 10 then increments to 11. c = 6 + 10 = 16. Finally, b is printed as 11.

questions.question: Which term refers to a storage location in memory used by an application to store data that can be changed during execution?
questions.explanation: Variables are named memory locations reserved to store data. Developers assign names to variables to access and manipulate the values they hold.

questions.question: What are the primary differences between the 'var' and 'dynamic' keywords in C#?

options.text: 'var' was introduced in C# 3.0, while 'dynamic' was introduced in C# 4.0
'var' is statically typed (resolved at compile time), 'dynamic' is resolved at runtime
'var' errors are caught during compilation, 'dynamic' errors only occur at runtime

questions.explanation: 'var' uses type inference at compile time. 'dynamic' bypasses compile-time type checking and is resolved by the DLR (Dynamic Language Runtime) at execution.

questions.question: Consider these initializations inside a method. Which statement is correct?
questions.code:
1. MyClass obj1; MyClass obj2 = null;
2. int i; int j = 0;
questions.explanation: In C#, local variables are not automatically initialized. Using 'obj1' or 'i' before assignment causes a compile error, whereas 'obj2' and 'j' have explicit initial values.

questions.question: What will be the values of 'a' and 'b' after the following code executes?
questions.explanation: Assignment expressions in C# return the assigned value. (b = 10) evaluates to 10, then 10 + 5 is 15, which is assigned to 'a'.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: c = (a--) - (++b). a-- uses 5, then a becomes 4. ++b increments 10 to 11. c = 5 - 11 = -6. b is now 11.
